- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or erratic, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overcorrection, reduce subsequent 3–5 days’ forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward 60–65 range after 3–5 consecutive high forecasts, apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or volatile, model often misreads trend; use 20-day moving average of true values as anchor for correction.
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days to reflect cooling sentiment.
